title: Chinese Upland kangkong: Characteristics
metaDescription: Chinese Upland kangkong: the kangkong variety, with its traits, ratings and where it grows best in the Philippines. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Chinese Upland kangkong is an open pollinated (grown from seed) kangkong variety. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Ramgo.

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Chinese Upland kangkong is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Key facts about Chinese Upland kangkong

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

The registry gives no day count or trial yield for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit kangkong fields most often: [golden apple snail](/pests/golden-apple-snail), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 25 to 30 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Leaves: somewhat firmer than lowland kangkong, on a more upright plant.
Grown in well drained soil without standing water, unlike paddy kangkong.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: sold as a Ramgo garden packet, the only evidence found is Ramgo's listing. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual kangkong on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Chinese Upland kangkong

Upland kangkong grows from seed on dry beds, and lowland kangkong from cuttings in wet ground. Both regrow after each cutting. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Fertilizer for vegetables](/blog/fertilizer-for-vegetables-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.a: Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Chinese Upland?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
